quotes: LeakGuard runs under its own service account svc-leakguard-valves and never uses staff accounts.
findings.model_reasoning: One quote shows a separate service account for LeakGuard. The log entry shows the action executed under a shared staff account instead, which conflicts with separation from staff login.

quotes: The account may close only the twelve isolation valves listed in annex B.
findings.model_reasoning: This quote limits the agent to a specific set of valve-closing actions, which shows permissions are scoped to its charter. The evidence does not mention formal review, but the limited permission itself is clearly in place.

quotes: Maria, operations lead, or the duty engineer approves each valve closure proposed by LeakGuard and can override or stop LeakGuard at any time.
findings.model_reasoning: This sentence names people who approve and can stop or override the agent’s actions. That directly satisfies the control.

quotes: After a closure, staff can reopen the valve manually from the console within 5 minutes.
findings.model_reasoning: This states the action can be reversed manually within a stated time. That meets the control.

quotes: Every LeakGuard action is written to the central log with time, account, action, target and result.
findings.model_reasoning: This quote lists automatic logging of every action and includes the required fields: time, identity/account, action, target, and result.

quotes: Logs are kept for 12 months and reviewed weekly by the duty engineer.
findings.model_reasoning: This states logs are retained for at least six months and are reviewed. Twelve months exceeds the minimum retention period.
